Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification: Atlas AI / Redwood

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier - quick follow-up with the high-level numbers from our side so you have context for sizing/pricing. We want to make sure we capture the right scope before you send a ballpark.

Summary of expected usage:
- Average tokens/day: 2-4M (roughly 60-120M/month)
- Typical sequence length: ~256 tokens (prompt + response)
- Concurrency: ~8-15 concurrent requests (mostly short chat-like interactions)
- Performance targets: p95 latency <200-300ms; occasional bursts to p95 ~1.2k tokens/sec

Model & infra notes:
- We'll be serving a quantized 70B variant (Open-style / Llama family) - not a 8k context model.
- We're open to A100 or H100 class GPUs if cost-effective and compatible with your runtime.

Budget / unit economics: looking for target price in the ballpark of $300-400 per 1M tokens (we understand dedicated capacity pricing is different from hosted).

Procurement timeline: procurement engaged; target decision in 4-6 weeks, POC ideally in next 2-4 weeks.

Next steps from our side: can you confirm a recommended reserved capacity (GPU type & count) + throughput estimate and a rough effective $/1M token range for that configuration? If you need more detail I can pull real telemetry from our staging traffic.

Thanks - Alex

Hi Alex - great to meet you on the call, and thanks for the clear summary. Looping in Marcus and Aditya to help size the dedicated pool.

Top-line recap and clarifying Qs so we size conservatively:
- Usage you shared (2-4M tokens/day; 60-120M/month) and the model shape (70B quantized, ~256 median seq) is helpful.
- Our preliminary config assumptions: 2x A100-80GB or 2x H100 (depending on performance needs) tends to be the right starting point for 8-15 concurrent chat-style requests at the latency targets you mentioned, with autoscale/burst for short peaks.

Questions we need to confirm to tighten the estimate:
1) Is the 2-4M tokens/day steady-state or bursty (e.g., most tokens in a few hours)?
2) Do you expect long-running generation (many 1k+ token responses) or are responses typically <512 tokens?
3) Do you plan to enable aggressive KV/prefix caching for repeated contexts (helps reduce costs a lot)?
4) Is end-to-end p95 latency target measured at your edge or from Redwood? Are you able to accept slightly higher p95 for heavy batch windows?

Ballpark $/1M tokens (very rough):
- 2x A100 (reserved) + Redwood managed runtime: ~$420-40 per 1M tokens (amortized infrastructure + support + network)
- 2x H100 (reserved) + Redwood managed runtime: ~$520-680 per 1M tokens (higher perf, higher amortized cost)

We can tighten those numbers once we have answers to the Qs above and a short telemetry sample. I attached our dedicated-pricing overview (PDF) with the assumptions we usually use for the amortization math and an example cost model.

Recommended next steps:
- You send a 48-72 hour staging traffic dump (or a representative sample) so we can run an initial sizing/throughput sim.
- We propose a 30-day POC on reserved capacity (2 GPUs) with load testing (we'll provide test harness) - allows us to validate throughput and effective $/1M tokens for your workload.
- If that looks good, we'll convert to a committed Dedicated plan with monthly billing / committed throughput.

I can do a 30-minute sync later this week to walk through assumptions - suggested times: Thu 10-11am PT or Fri 2-3pm PT.

Thanks,

From: Alex Smith <alex.smith@atlasai.com>

Thanks Marissa - answers inline below.

1) Steady-state vs bursty: Mostly steady-state across business hours, but we have ~30% of daily volume in a 3-hour peak window.
2) Response length: Typical responses are 128-384 tokens; long tails are rare but do happen (~1-2% of requests >1k tokens).
3) Caching: Yes - we plan to use prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (customer support flows), so effective token counts should be lower for repeat traffic.
4) Latency: p95 target is measured end-to-end from our app. We can accept slightly higher p95 during heavy batch windows as long as p50/p90 stays low.

Procurement note: procurement team will want a 30-day trial POC and a clear committed pricing estimate to vet internally. We can provide a 72-hour telemetry sample this week.

One other ask: can you indicate the throughput (tokens/sec) you expect from the 2x A100 and 2x H100 configs for the quantized 70B model (assuming 256 sequence length and ~12 concurrency)? If you can give p50/p95 throughput that helps our SREs plan.

Appreciate it - Alex

Alex - thanks for the quick clarifications and the staging telemetry offer. Marcus ran a short sim and here are our preliminary throughput estimates for a quantized 70B workload (256 seq, ~12 concurrency):

- 2x A100-80GB (Redwood runtime, optimized kernels): p50 ~600 tokens/sec, p95 ~1,000 tokens/sec (with bursts above 1.2k for short windows)
- 2x H100 (Redwood runtime, faster matmuls): p50 ~850 tokens/sec, p95 ~1,400 tokens/sec

Notes:
- These numbers assume typical batching and KV cache savings - actual effective tokens/sec for your production traffic will likely be +10-30% if prefix caching hits are high.
- If you need consistent p95 under 300ms for 12 concurrent chat requests, we recommend starting with 2x H100 for headroom.

Updated effective $/1M tokens (refined):
- 2x A100 reserved POC: ~$390-40 per 1M tokens (assumes 30-day reserved baseline + managed runtime)
- 2x H100 reserved POC: ~$480-620 per 1M tokens

Proposed commercial POC:
- 30-day POC on 2x H100 (recommended for latency headroom), Redwood provides test harness + load script.
- Redwood will run a throughput validation and provide a final effective $/1M tokens based on measured effective token consumption.

- If the POC validates, we will provide a dedicated contract (monthly committed capacity) with tiered pricing and rollover credits for unused baseline.

Next steps: please share the 72-hour telemetry dump (or grant a short read-only link) and confirm whether procurement is OK with a 30-day POC on a reserved pool. We can kick off paperwork (SOW) the same day.

Available to talk Fri 2-3pm PT if you want to go over the numbers with Marcus + Aditya.
